- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak by 5–10% to account for overreaction.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% upward bias to reflect mean reversion toward higher levels.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.25+ in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast volatility by 10–15% to avoid overfitting to noise.  
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 10+ days, apply a 1–2% upward correction to reflect lagged sentiment influence.
